title: Term vs Whole Life Insurance: The $1M Question
description:
Term vs whole life insurance: for the same $1 million payout, Policygenius sample rates for a healthy 30-year-old man were $48.89 a month for 20-year term life and $920 a month for whole life, nearly 19 times more. Term covers a set number of years and then ends; whole life lasts for life and builds cash value. Which fits depends on how long someone relies on your income.

Source: Policygenius, "How much does a $1 million life insurance policy cost?" (rate illustration valid as of Oct 1, 2024). Term rates: average of 11 carriers, non-smokers, Preferred health class. Whole life rates: sample policy paid up at age 100 through MassMutual, non-smokers, Preferred Plus health class. For a 30-year-old woman the same tables show $36.90 vs $801. Our 20-year totals multiply those monthly premiums by 240 months; they ignore the cash value a whole life policy builds and any dividends. Real premiums depend on your age, health, insurer, state and the date. This is a general explainer, not insurance or financial advice; compare quotes and policy documents before you buy.

scenes.say: Same million dollar payout: forty-nine a month, or nine hundred twenty. Why?
Policy Genius sample rates, healthy thirty-year-old man: nearly nineteen times more.
Term covers set years, then ends. Whole life lasts for life, building cash value.
Twenty years of premiums: about twelve thousand dollars, versus two hundred twenty-one thousand.
Part of that builds cash value. Term pays nothing if you outlive it.
So which is better? It depends on one question.
How long will someone depend on your income?

visual.label: How long do others rely on your income?

scenes.say: A fixed number of years? Term fits. A lifelong need? Whole life fits.
Need first. Otherwise you're just comparing...
